effective_power_read: Phase-1 iso_rating 7 overstates this. Applying P5 (setup tax) and P8 (Nullify semantics): the assassin payoff is gated behind a TWO-step transformation ramp, not available turn 1. Base kit (cell1 30 Piercing, +5/transform capped at +10 = max 40; cell2 stun+shatter; cell3 Absorption package) is a modest single-target poker — solid mid. The efficient finisher floor flagged by Phase-1 (cell8 Death Beam: 25 Piercing-bypass + Isolate, 1 Blue, CD0) only EXISTS after 2 transformations; cell7 Kamehameha (40 Piercing-bypass) is CD2 — committal (P3). Each transform requires landing Absorption (CD1) then either killing the target under it OR the opponent declining to break a 25-point Nullify over 2 turns — a competent attacker simply punches through the barrier (consume path, no trigger), denying the passive route, so full power is genuinely opponent-gated. P8 confirmed in components: barrier_effect is checked in character_component.gd:729 check_damage_against_barriers against the ATTACKER's barriers (line 730 attacker.get_barrier_effects), so Absorption's 25 Nullify reduces the ENEMY's OUTGOING damage = offensive control, exactly the documented reverse-Shield — not a bug. P1/P2: the ramp engine (Absorption) is all-Random (always payable), base specific burden is light (1 Green / 1 Blue), so throughput isn't heavily color-taxed — but throughput is also modest (10x3 Rain, 25/40 bypass). P4: the only 'execute' is a stun-if-<=30HP rider — a finisher condition, low weight, no instakill. The two-path ramp (P1 flag #2) is fairer-than-typical-ramp reliability, but the online payoff is efficient-not-oppressive. Net: dependable B core, real setup tax, no oppressive ceiling.

Effective read: peak ~50 anti-invuln delayed nuke behind Heavy Metal + a piercing-pressure loop behind a setup turn = no glaring strength or weakness, B not A.

effective_power_read: Delay-engine control/support, not a burst threat. hashirama5 plants a permanent system delay_eff(mag1, Harmful) on himself (hashirama5.gd:22-26), so every Harmful skill he casts is deferred: it does NOT execute on cast, it fires later when its DELAYED_SKILL effect ticks to duration 1 (battle_manager.gd:1169). The payoff is therefore back-loaded (3 turns base, 5 turns once Creation enhances mag to 2). The passive pays a fixed 5 Shield (team) + 5 Piercing (AoE) per skill currently pending each turn (hashirama5.gd:55-63), with no hidden multiplier — strictly linear, looped `for i in range(total_delays)`, no per_stack/stack_mag (confirmed hashirama5.gd:25 only). Principle 5 (setup tax): turn 1 does nothing; the engine needs 2-3 setup turns and only spikes once multiple skills are pending AND Creation's 7-turn mark is up for the enhanced 5-heal/5-Affliction/random-stun bonuses. Principles 1-2 (color burden): three of four active skills cost Red (Pollen Red+Random, Strangle Red, Creation Red — abilities_data.json:3447-3502) — a real mono-Red tax that gates how many delays you can keep pending and is color-screwable. The Phase-1 'unbounded loop' is real in code (Creation CD0 re-extends all delays, hashirama3.gd:30-36) but bounded: each re-extension trades the actual Pollen/Strangle burst for small 5/5 tick value, Piercing is only 5/skill, and you must keep paying Red. Net: resilient, hard-to-fully-shut-off sustained AoE shield+chip+soft CC once online, but slow, telegraphed, color-screwable, and low per-tick numbers. Top-of-fair A, not S (not cheap/uncounterable/oppressive); the heavy setup+color tax discounts an otherwise-overloaded kit down to fair.

effective_power_read: Single-target control/disruptor, NOT the A/iso-7 the Phase-1 flags imply. Specific-color burden is the heaviest tax in the game (Principle 1/2): kakashi1 = Green+Blue, kakashi2 = White+Red, so across the 4-skill bar he touches ALL FOUR colors and is genuinely color-screwable on any turn. Offense is all-Piercing (DR-agnostic) but the raw numbers are modest: 40 (kakashi1) + 30 (kakashi2), each CD1. The kakashi2 100%-nullify is a strong single-target neutralize and IS implemented (character_component.gd:725-726 multiplies attacker's outgoing damage by 1.0-mag = 0), but it only blanks ONE skill and the target chooses when to spend it; the energy drain riding alongside is tempo-flavor not a wincon (Principle 6). Team protection is real (counter + self/ally invuln) but the invuln is CD4 — very committal, available ~every 4 turns (Principle 3). The uncounterable/unreflectable passive (kakashi5, implemented via ignore_effect_effect on COUNTER_RECEIVE/USE) is a clean but narrow hard-counter to reactive kits (Principle 7-adjacent). High pilot difficulty (color tax) + modest damage + a CD4 protection button = solid B core, not top-of-fair. Note kakashi3's countered enemy is SUPPOSED to take 25 piercing but doesn't (bug below), so his realized power is slightly below even the listed kit.

tuning_suggestion: Fix the bug, not the balance: add a custom counter callback to kakashi3 that deals 25 piercing to the countered enemy (context['owner']) before chaining default_counter_trigger(context), matching the advertised text. No power numbers need changing — the kit is fair at B once the described effect actually fires. If anything, post-fix he is still a clean B (heavy 4-color tax + CD4 invuln keep him honest), so no nerf needed; leave damage 40/30, nullify 100%, invuln CD4 as-is.

effective_power_read: Phase-1 rated 7.5 / possible-overtuned on a wide 11-ability kit with permanent silence, shield-shatter AoE, and an 8-turn delay nuke. Applying the principles, this recalibrates to a strong-but-fair A, not an outlier. (1) Setup tax (P5): the 4 visible slots are Control stances (korra1-4: 1-Random, CD2, invisible) that place a single-class counter AND swap the slot to its attack form (korra5-8). The attacks are NOT freely available — you spend a tempo turn unlocking each one. (2) Specific-color burden (P1/P2): every attack carries real specific cost — Fire Fist Red:1, Air Wave White:1, Earth Area Green:2, Water Arm Blue:1 — and the damage (25 aff / 20 pierce AoE / 40-20 shatter AoE / 15+stun) is modest-to-solid, paid for by color commitment and color-screwable. (3) The two scary tools are Avatar-gated (P5, heavy time-to-online): Energybending (perm uncleansable silence, korra9, effect_component.gd:754 dur=-1 + cleansable=false) and Gate Open (40 pierce AoE + 8-turn delay, korra10) are ONLY reachable after Korra Avatar State activates — which needs 5 same-element skill uses AND is once-per-game (korra11:74,80-90). Gate Open is additionally CD8 with a 4-specific-color cost (Green+Blue+White+Red = max color burden). (4) The two piercing/affliction sources (korra5 affliction, korra6/korra10 piercing) do bypass mitigation but at small-to-mid numbers. Net: a top-of-fair adaptive controller — high ceiling backed by genuine setup tax, specific-color load, CD2 base tempo, and once-per-game gating on the oppressive pieces. A, not S.

effective_power_read: Phase-1 iso 7.5 / "over outlier" overstates him. No execute, no instakill (Principle 4) — peak burst is a 30 Piercing that requires spending a prior turn on megumi1 to place the mark, so it's gated by setup tax (Principle 5). Two of the key skills cost specific Red, a genuine color-screw tax (Principle 1/2) that partly pays for the Piercing. The megumi5 passive re-rolls 1/4 which class (Physical/Energy/Mental/Affliction) skills 1/2/4 reference each turn; verified in character_component.is_stunned (1467-1488) and is_invuln (1493-1515): megumi1 uses exclusion_targets=[rolled class] so it stuns ALL skills EXCEPT the rolled class (always lands broadly), megumi2 uses ability_targets=[rolled class] so it stuns ONLY that class (narrow, can be dead vs an enemy with no skill of that class), megumi4 invuln-to-non-rolled-class. So the Phase-1 'RNG whiffs the CC' flag is directionally right — the stun is class-gated and RNG-shuffled, weaker and less reliable than the bare word 'stun' implies — but it never whiffs to literally nothing.
